Find Your Solution

We Treat Every Condition

Missing teeth, loose dentures, bone loss, infections \u2013 we've seen it all and we have the solution.

Free Consultation1-Hour Consultation — £80Call 020 71833573

\u2713 15+ Conditions Treated \u00b7 \u2713 Complex Cases Welcome \u00b7 \u2713 0% Finance*

Restoring Smiles, Regardless of Complexity

Below is the full list of conditions suitable for single implants, multiple implants, or All-on-4 full-arch solutions. Our experienced team is equipped to handle everything from straightforward replacements to complex full-mouth rehabilitations. View our prices →

1. Missing Teeth (Single or Multiple)

Whether you’re missing one tooth or several, dental implants restore appearance, function, and confidence.

Learn More

2. Failing or Damaged Teeth

Teeth that are cracked, heavily decayed, broken at the gum line, or beyond repair can be replaced with implants. In many cases, hopeless teeth can be removed and replaced on the same day.

Learn More

3. Loose or Ill-Fitting Dentures

For patients who struggle with loose dentures, painful rubbing, difficulty chewing, or dentures that fall out. Implants or All-on-4 offer a secure, fixed alternative.

Learn More

4. Severe Tooth Loss / Full Arch Tooth Loss

Ideal for patients who have lost most or all teeth in an arch. All-on-4 provides fixed teeth on the same day, replacing removable dentures entirely.

Learn More

5. Gum Disease Leading to Tooth Loss

Advanced periodontal disease often results in teeth becoming loose or falling out. Once the gum disease is treated and stabilised, implants can restore full function.

Learn More

6. Bone Loss in the Jaw

Patients with bone loss due to long-term missing teeth may need bone grafting, sinus lifts, or ridge preservation. All-on-4 is also suitable for many bone-loss cases because it uses tilted implants to maximise remaining bone.

Learn More

7. Fractured or Root-Filled Teeth

Root-canal-treated teeth that keep failing, cracking, or causing infections can be replaced with long-lasting implants.

Learn More

8. Infected or Abscessed Teeth

If a tooth is infected or has recurrent abscesses, it can be extracted and replaced with an implant once healed. In some cases, immediate implants are possible.

Learn More

9. Congenitally Missing Teeth

Common for lateral incisors and premolars (teeth that never developed). Implants offer a long-term, fixed solution instead of bridges or dentures.

Learn More

10. Worn, Broken or Damaged Bridges

Patients with old bridges that keep breaking or causing problems can switch to implants for significantly more stability.

Learn More

11. Bite Problems Caused by Missing Teeth

Issues such as collapsed bite, shifting teeth, difficulty chewing, or overloading remaining teeth. Implants help restore proper bite and balance.

Learn More

12. Patients Unable to Tolerate Dentures

Some people experience gag reflex, sore spots, speech issues, or dentures that feel unnatural. All-on-4 fixed teeth eliminate these problems.

Learn More

13. Failed Previous Implants

If your previous implants failed due to infection, poor positioning, trauma, or bone loss, we can assess and provide corrective implant treatment (Re-treatment Cases).

Learn More

14. Teeth Lost Due to Trauma or Accidents

Implants restore aesthetics and function after injuries caused by sports, falls, or accidents.

Learn More

15. Jawbone Shrinkage After Years of Dentures

All-on-4 is ideal for long-term denture wearers who have lost significant bone over time.

Learn More

16. Collapsing Bite

Progressive tooth wear or missing teeth can reduce bite height, affecting chewing function, tooth stability, and facial appearance. Restorative treatments and implants may help restore bite stability.

Learn More

17. Dental Implant Infection

Infection may develop in the tissues surrounding a dental implant, causing swelling, discomfort, or bleeding. Early professional assessment can help protect implant stability.

Learn More

18. Dental Implant Pain

Discomfort around a dental implant may occur during healing or develop later. Professional assessment can help identify the cause and determine appropriate treatment.

Learn More

19. Dentures Moving While Eating

Denture movement during meals may be caused by jawbone changes or poor fit. Professional assessment can help identify options to improve stability, including implant-retained dentures.

Learn More

20. Dentures Without Stability

Dentures that lack adequate support may shift during speaking or eating. Professional assessment can help identify options from denture relining to implant-retained solutions.

Learn More

21. Difficulty Chewing Due To Missing Teeth

Missing teeth can reduce chewing efficiency and affect diet and nutrition. Professional assessment can help identify suitable tooth replacement options including dental implants.

Learn More

22. Failed Bone Graft

A bone graft may not always integrate as expected. Professional assessment can help determine the cause and whether further treatment or implant planning may be appropriate.

Learn More

23. Failed Dental Implant

A dental implant may fail to integrate or develop complications over time. Professional assessment can help identify the cause and determine appropriate treatment options.

Learn More

24. Failing Dental Bridge

A dental bridge may become loose, unstable or less functional over time. Professional assessment can help determine whether repair, replacement or implant treatment may be appropriate.

Learn More

25. Failing Root Canal Tooth

A tooth that has previously received root canal treatment may develop new complications. Professional assessment can help determine whether the tooth can be preserved or whether replacement may be needed.

Learn More

26. Loose Dental Implant

A dental implant that shows movement or instability may require professional assessment to determine whether the issue involves the crown, connecting components, or the implant fixture itself.

Learn More

27. Loose Dental Bridge

A dental bridge that no longer fits securely may become loose or unstable over time. Professional assessment can help determine whether repair, replacement or implant-supported treatment may be appropriate.

Learn More

28. Loose Implant Crown

An implant crown that feels loose, clicks, or moves when chewing may require professional assessment to determine whether the screw, abutment, or crown itself needs repair or replacement.

Learn More

29. Loose Implant Screw

The abutment screw connecting an implant crown to the fixture may loosen over time due to bite forces or component wear. Professional assessment can determine whether the screw requires tightening, replacement, or further treatment.

Learn More

30. Old Dental Implant Problems

Older dental implants may develop complications over time due to wear, bone changes, or gum health issues. Professional assessment can help determine whether maintenance, repair, or revision treatment may be appropriate.

Learn More

31. Painful Dentures

Dentures that cause pain, sore gums, or discomfort when eating may require professional assessment to determine whether adjustment, relining, replacement, or implant-supported alternatives may improve comfort and stability.

Learn More

32. Peri-implant Mucositis

Peri-implant mucositis is an early inflammatory condition affecting the gum tissue around a dental implant. Professional assessment and treatment may help manage inflammation and support long-term implant health.

Learn More

33. Peri-implantitis

Peri-implantitis is an inflammatory condition involving infection and bone loss around a dental implant. Early professional assessment may help manage the condition and support continued implant stability.

Learn More

34. Severely Worn Teeth

Severely worn teeth may result from grinding, acid erosion, or long-term wear. Professional assessment can help identify appropriate restorative or implant-based treatment options.

Learn More

35. Sunken Face From Missing Teeth

Missing teeth may lead to jawbone loss and gradual changes in facial structure. Professional assessment can help determine whether dental implants may support oral function and facial appearance.

Learn More
